$comment: The single source of truth for the native<->web bridge.
Nothing here is written by hand on either side: tools/gen_bridge.py emits
the C++ request/response structs, the handler interface and the dispatch
table, and the TypeScript types and typed call wrappers. Adding a method
below and rebuilding makes the C++ fail to compile until it is implemented,
which is the point -- the schema cannot drift away from either end.
Field types: string, int, double, bool, or the name of an entry in
"types". Add "array": true for a list, "optional": true for a field that
A capability groups methods and events and carries a version. The UI reads
that version from shell.getCapabilities() and degrades when something it
wants is missing or older than it needs. SONORA_DISABLE_CAPS turns one off
at runtime so the degraded path can be exercised on demand instead of only
on an old build. A capability marked "required" cannot be turned off: with
shell.getCapabilities() gone there is nothing left to negotiate with.

PlayerState.summary: Everything the interface needs to draw the transport, in one object.

fields.name: state
fields.summary: idle, loading, playing, paused or stopped.

fields.name: trackIndex
fields.summary: Position in the queue, or -1 when nothing is loaded.

fields.name: queueSize
fields.summary: How many tracks are queued.

fields.name: queueVersion
fields.summary: Increments on every change to the queue's contents. This is what a page watches to know when to ask for the queue again: the size and the index cannot say it, because replacing one track with another changes neither, and a page trusting them draws the old title over the new audio.

fields.name: positionMs
fields.summary: How far into the current track the listener is.

fields.name: durationMs
fields.summary: Length of the current track, 0 when it is not known.

fields.name: volume
fields.summary: Linear gain, 0 to 1.

fields.name: currentPath
fields.summary: The current track's path, empty when nothing is loaded.

fields.name: underruns
fields.summary: Callbacks the decode thread was late for, since startup.

fields.name: trackChanges
fields.summary: Gapless joins performed inside a callback.

fields.name: lastError
fields.summary: The last track that could not be opened, empty when there was none.

Capability.summary: One capability, as the shell currently reports it.

fields.name: name
fields.summary: Capability name, as used in a method's prefix.

fields.name: version
fields.summary: Version the shell implements.

fields.name: enabled
fields.summary: False when this build or this run has it switched off.

LibraryTrack.summary: One track as the library knows it. Note what is absent: the file's path. The page addresses a track by id and never learns where it lives, which is what removed the 'open whatever this string says' boundary week 6 had to guard by hand.

fields.name: id
fields.summary: Stable for as long as the file stays where it is. The only way the page refers to a track.

fields.name: title
fields.summary: From the tags, or the file name when there is no title tag.

fields.name: artist
fields.summary: Track artist.

fields.name: album
fields.summary: Album name, empty when untagged.

fields.name: albumArtist
fields.summary: Album artist, falling back to the track artist.

fields.name: trackNumber
fields.summary: 0 when untagged.

fields.name: discNumber
fields.summary: 0 when untagged.

fields.name: year
fields.summary: 0 when untagged.

fields.name: durationMs
fields.summary: Length in milliseconds, read from the audio properties.

fields.name: artUrl
fields.summary: Where to get the cover, or empty when the file has none. Built by the shell so the page never assembles a URL out of a hash.

LibraryAlbum.summary: A row of the album list. Not a table in the index: a grouping of tracks. See ADR 0007.

fields.name: album
fields.summary: Album name.

fields.name: albumArtist
fields.summary: Album artist, which is what albums are grouped by.

fields.name: year
fields.summary: Earliest year among its tracks, 0 when untagged.

fields.name: trackCount
fields.summary: How many tracks the index has for it.

fields.name: durationMs
fields.summary: Total length.

fields.name: artUrl
fields.summary: Cover of any track that has one, empty when none do.

LibraryStatus.summary: What the library is doing, and what it has. Sent as an event during a scan and available on demand, the same shape both ways -- like PlayerState, and for the same reason.

fields.name: root
fields.summary: The folder being indexed, empty when none has been chosen yet.

fields.name: trackCount
fields.summary: Tracks in the index right now.

fields.name: albumCount
fields.summary: Albums in the index right now.

fields.name: artistCount
fields.summary: Distinct track artists.

fields.name: scanning
fields.summary: True while a scan is in flight.

fields.name: filesSeen
fields.summary: Audio files the current or last scan walked past.

fields.name: filesRead
fields.summary: ...of which the tags were actually read. Far smaller than filesSeen on a rescan, which is the incremental scan working.

fields.name: added
fields.summary: Rows added by the current or last scan.

fields.name: updated
fields.summary: Rows updated.

fields.name: removed
fields.summary: Rows dropped because the file is gone.

fields.name: failed
fields.summary: Files that could not be read. Counted, not fatal.

fields.name: lastError
fields.summary: Why the last scan could not start or finish, empty when it could.

QueueEntry.summary: One entry of the play queue, resolved through the library so the page can draw a title rather than a path.

fields.name: index
fields.summary: Position in the queue.

fields.name: trackId
fields.summary: 0 when this entry is not in the library, which happens for a file queued by --play.

fields.name: title
fields.summary: Track title, or the file name when the index has never seen this file.

fields.name: artist
fields.summary: Track artist, empty when unknown.

fields.name: durationMs
fields.summary: Length, 0 when unknown.

fields.name: artUrl
fields.summary: Cover, empty when there is none.

capabilities.name: shell
capabilities.summary: Information about the native shell hosting this page.

methods.name: getVersion
methods.summary: Versions of the shell and of the embedded browser.

methods.name: echo
methods.summary: Round-trips a string through the native side. Exists to prove the bridge end to end, and to exercise the failure path: an empty message is rejected.

params.name: repeat
params.summary: How many copies to return. Defaults to 1, maximum 64.

result.name: lengthBytes
result.summary: Length of the returned message in UTF-8 bytes.

methods.name: getCapabilities
methods.summary: What this shell exposes right now, including what is switched off. The first call a page should make: everything else depends on the answer.

result.name: capabilities
result.summary: Every capability the build knows about, enabled or not.

capabilities.name: player
capabilities.summary: The transport: a queue, a position and the controls over both. Every method is a command that returns once the player has been told, not once the sound has changed -- the state event is what says what actually happened. Version 2 because enqueue changed shape: it takes library ids instead of a file path, which is a break, and a page compiled against version 1 has to be told rather than left to fail one call at a time.

methods.name: getState
methods.summary: The whole transport state. Sent as an event too; this is for the first paint, before any event has arrived.

methods.name: enqueue
methods.summary: Adds library tracks to the queue, in the order given. A list rather than one id because queueing an album is one call, not fifty; and ids rather than paths because a path from the renderer is a boundary somebody has to defend, while an id is either in the index or it is not.

params.name: trackIds
params.summary: Library ids. An id the index does not know is an error, and none of the list is queued.

params.name: replace
params.summary: Clears the queue first. Defaults to false.

result.name: queueSize
result.summary: How many tracks are queued now.

methods.name: getQueue
methods.summary: What is in the queue, resolved through the library. Not an event: the queue changes when the page changes it, and player.state already says when its size or position moved -- which is when a page that cares should ask again.

methods.name: clearQueue
methods.summary: Empties the queue and stops.

methods.name: play
methods.summary: Starts, or resumes after a pause. Starting from idle plays the head of the queue.

methods.name: pause
methods.summary: Fades out over about twenty milliseconds and then stops consuming. Instant, and not a click.

methods.name: stop
methods.summary: Lets go of the current track. The queue survives.

methods.name: next
methods.summary: Skips to the next track. Not the same as a gapless join: this one is meant to be heard.

methods.name: previous
methods.summary: Restarts the current track when more than three seconds have played, and goes back one otherwise.

methods.name: jumpTo
methods.summary: Plays the queue entry at this position. Absolute, unlike next and previous, so it also starts playback when nothing is playing -- which is what clicking a row of the queue has to do. An index the queue does not have is ignored rather than refused: the queue can change between the page drawing a row and somebody clicking it.

methods.name: seek
methods.summary: Moves to a position in the current track.

methods.name: setVolume
methods.summary: Linear gain, clamped to 0..1, applied as a ramp so it cannot click.

events.name: state
events.summary: The transport moved. Emitted far faster than it is delivered -- the position changes every buffer and a person reads it four times a second -- which is exactly the shape the coalescer was built for in week 4.

payload.name: player
payload.summary: The whole state, not a delta: a page that missed an event must not end up with a stale half of one.

capabilities.name: library
capabilities.summary: The index of what is on disk. Every method here is a read except scan, and every read is answered from SQLite rather than from the filesystem -- which is what makes a list of fifty thousand tracks a query and not a directory walk.

methods.name: getStatus
methods.summary: What the library has and whether it is scanning. The first call a page makes into this capability: an empty index and a scan in flight look the same from a track count alone.

methods.name: scan
methods.summary: Starts a scan and returns immediately -- it does not wait for it, because a scan of a real music folder is minutes and a bridge call must not be. Progress arrives as library.status events. Asking while one is already running is not an error; it says so and changes nothing.

params.name: path
params.summary: Folder to index. Absent means the folder already in use, which is how a rescan is asked for.

result.name: started
result.summary: False when a scan was already in flight.

methods.name: listTracks
methods.summary: A page of every track, in album order. Paged because the page draws a window of rows, not a whole library, and a call that returns fifty thousand records to display forty of them is a call that stutters.

params.name: limit
params.summary: How many rows. Defaults to 500, maximum 5000.

result.name: total
result.summary: How many there are in all, so the page can size its scrollbar without asking for the rest.

methods.name: listAlbums
methods.summary: Every album, ordered by album artist. A grouping, computed on the spot.

methods.name: listArtists
methods.summary: Every distinct track artist, in order.

methods.name: albumTracks
methods.summary: The tracks of one album, in disc and track order. Both parts of the identity are needed: two different artists can have an album called Greatest Hits, and they are not one album.

params.name: album
params.summary: Album name, exactly as listAlbums gave it.

params.name: albumArtist
params.summary: Album artist, exactly as listAlbums gave it.

methods.name: artistTracks
methods.summary: Everything by one artist, grouped by album.

params.name: artist
params.summary: Artist name, exactly as listArtists gave it.

methods.name: search
methods.summary: Full-text search over titles, artists and albums, best match first, with the last word treated as a prefix so the list narrows while somebody is still typing. Whatever is in the box is text: no part of it is syntax, however it is spelled.

params.name: query
params.summary: What the person typed. An empty or punctuation-only query returns nothing rather than everything.

result.name: tracks
result.summary: Ranked by how well they match.

events.name: status
events.summary: The library changed: a scan started, made progress or finished. Coalesced, because a scan of ten thousand files would otherwise post ten thousand events at a page that can use four a second -- the same producer/consumer mismatch as the transport, handled by the same machinery.

payload.name: library
payload.summary: The whole status, not a delta.

capabilities.name: diagnostics
capabilities.summary: Numbers about the running process. Present in every build, and the one capability a deployment might reasonably switch off, which makes it the test subject for negotiation.

methods.name: getMetrics
methods.summary: A snapshot of the bridge's own counters.

result.name: uptimeMs
result.summary: Milliseconds since the shell finished starting.

result.name: eventsDelivered
result.summary: Events that actually reached the page.

result.name: eventsCoalesced
result.summary: Events replaced by a newer one before they were sent. posted = delivered + coalesced + whatever is still pending.

events.name: heartbeat
events.summary: Emitted far faster than it is delivered, on purpose: it is the shape every later event has -- playback position, buffer level, download progress -- where the producer runs at its own rate and the UI only needs the newest value.

payload.name: sequence
payload.summary: Increments once per emission, including the ones that never arrive. Gaps are the coalescing, visible from the page.

payload.name: uptimeMs
payload.summary: Milliseconds since the shell finished starting.
